analysis.title: Microchip Technology Inc. (MCHP): Cyclical recovery and favorable end-market trends remain intact despite softer guidance
key_insights: GS expects MCHP to trade lower after a quarter in line with the Street but with FY3Q27 guidance below the Street. Investor expectations were elevated going into the print after management commentary on restocking, strong margin guidance and solid results from analog peers.

FY3Q27 revenue was guided to a $1.61bn midpoint (down 1% QoQ), below GS at $1.65bn and the Street at $1.63bn. Management said the outlook is above normal seasonality of down 3%-5% QoQ, but the comparison is affected by $53mn of unusual FY2Q revenue (licensing, price increases, contract revenue in roughly equal parts).

Non-GAAP gross margin was guided to 64.5% for the December quarter, below GS at 66.2% and the Street at 66.5%. The reasons given are constrained supply of high-margin leading-edge products and higher input costs. GS notes it is consistent with the company's 65% long-term model.

FY2Q27 revenue was $1.62bn, in line with GS at $1.62bn and the Street at $1.61bn. Non-GAAP gross margin was 66.5% against 66.6% for GS and the Street. Operating margin was 39.5% against 39.3% for GS and 39.1% for the Street. EPS was $0.97 against $0.96 for GS and $0.94 for the Street.

By segment, microcontroller revenue of $775mn missed GS at $799mn and the Street at $803mn. Analog at $459mn beat GS at $444mn and the Street at $440mn. Other at $388mn beat GS at $374mn and the Street at $365mn.

Gross margin rose about 280bps QoQ to 66.5%. The company said $53mn of high-margin infrequent items benefited the quarter. Management has not made another round of price increases to offset higher input costs, but is contemplating them.

Management sees signs of broad-based inventory restocking across distribution partners. Supply is tightening for products with outsourced testing or manufacturing, lead times are lengthening, and some leading-edge customer demand cannot be filled. Internal utilization is rising but remains well below 100%.

GS cut its 12-month price target to $100 from $115, using a 22x P/E (down from 26x on lower peer multiples) on unchanged normalized EPS of $4.50. It reiterates Buy and argues the Street under-models the recovery over the next 12-18 months because MCHP shipments have fallen the farthest from pre-COVID levels among GS analog coverage.
GS cut EPS estimates by about 4% on average: FY27E $3.70 from $3.75, FY28E $4.60 from $4.80, FY29E $5.10 from $5.40. Gross margin estimates fall 72-86bps across the three years.

GS sees a limited negative read-across to the analog group because most peers have already reported. The most direct read-across is to TXN (Sell) and ADI (Buy) because of their relatively high industrial exposure.

market_movers.rationale: Target cut to $100 from $115 on a lower peer multiple (22x vs 26x) with normalized EPS of $4.50 unchanged. GS keeps Buy, citing a cyclical recovery the Street under-models.
GS expects the most direct read-across from MCHP's softer guidance to fall on TXN because of high industrial exposure. The note describes the group read-across as limited.
ADI is named alongside TXN as most exposed to a read-across given its relatively high industrial exposure. The overall read-across is described as limited.

sector_views.rationale: GS sees a limited negative read-across from MCHP's guidance because most peers have already reported. Restocking signs and an industrial-led recovery remain supportive.

earnings_insights: MCHP FY2Q27 reported 11/5: revenue $1.62bn (non-GAAP, excl. SBC) vs GS $1.62bn and Street $1.61bn. Gross margin 66.5% vs 66.6% for GS and the Street. Operating margin 39.5% vs GS 39.3% and Street 39.1%. EPS $0.97 (excl. SBC) vs GS $0.96 and Street $0.94.

MCHP FY2Q27 reported segments: microcontrollers $775mn (GS est $799mn, Street est $803mn), analog $459mn (GS est $444mn, Street est $440mn), other $388mn (GS est $374mn, Street est $365mn). Reported revenue rose 9.2% QoQ and 42.2% YoY.

MCHP FY3Q27 guidance (midpoint, excl. SBC): revenue $1.606bn (range $1.573bn-$1.638bn) vs GS est $1.648bn and Street est $1.628bn. Gross margin 64.5% vs GS est 66.2% and Street est 66.5%. Operating margin 37.8% vs GS est 39.4% and Street est 39.0%. EPS $0.91 (range $0.87-$0.95) vs GS est $0.98 and Street est $0.95.

FY2Q27 results included $53mn of unusual revenue (higher licensing, price increases and contract revenue in roughly equal parts) and $53mn of high-margin infrequent items in gross margin. Normal seasonality for FY3Q is down 3%-5% QoQ.

GS new vs old estimates (excl. SBC): FY27E revenue $6,431mn (old $6,472mn), EPS $3.70 (old $3.75). FY28E revenue $7,481mn (old $7,616mn), EPS $4.60 (old $4.80). FY29E revenue $8,321mn (old $8,589mn), EPS $5.10 (old $5.40).

trade_ideas.description: Buy MCHP, 12-month price target $100 (22x P/E on normalized EPS of $4.50), 53.8% upside from $64.85
trade_ideas.rationale: GS believes the Street under-estimates the magnitude of the cyclical recovery over the next 3-5 quarters because MCHP shipments have fallen the farthest from pre-COVID levels among its analog coverage.
trade_ideas.risk: Timing of the analog and MCU recovery, and inventory on the balance sheet could delay margin expansion relative to peers.

risk_factors: Timing of the analog and microcontroller recovery.
Inventory on the balance sheet could delay MCHP's margin expansion relative to peers.
Supply constraints on outsourced testing and manufacturing, with lengthening lead times, limit shipments of leading-edge products.
Higher input costs without offsetting price increases pressure gross margin, guided to 64.5% for the December quarter.

tension_points.bull_case: GS expects broad-based industrial, datacenter and mil/aerospace demand, restocking at distributors and an improving product portfolio to drive stronger growth than peers, with the Street under-modeling a recovery over 12-18 months.
tension_points.bear_case: FY3Q27 guidance for revenue, gross margin, operating margin and EPS is below the Street, supply is constrained on leading-edge products, input costs are higher, and expectations were elevated going into the print.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Timing of the analog and MCU recovery slipping, or inventory on the balance sheet delaying margin expansion relative to peers.

theme_stances.key_argument: The Street under-estimates the magnitude of the potential cyclical recovery because MCHP shipments have fallen the farthest from pre-COVID levels among GS analog coverage.
theme_stances.evidence: the Street continues to under-model the fundamental recovery
